blocker.summary: r446 re-examined sub_821CC508's own decompilation (already in hand since r441/r443) around the confirmed failure site (+6171) and found it is the exhaustion point of a 5-attempt retry loop, not a direct failure: a real async read (sub_821F4E70, a ReadFile-equivalent) is checked via a GetLastError-equivalent (func_0x821f50a0/sub_821F50A0); success, no-error, or ERROR_IO_PENDING-style 0x3e5 all continue normally, anything else decrements a retry counter (initialized to 5) and retries via a goto, only giving up (logging via sub_821D4988, r445, then returning -1) once the counter hits zero. This read is sub_821CC508's OWN file operation, independent of sub_821CC008's separate file-enumeration branch that r445 already showed is not taken on this run -- both functions share a common resource table (iRam8293b94c, 16-byte entries) but make their own separate file calls. Live breakpoints on sub_821F50A0 (the GetLastError-equivalent) across several of its call sites captured a CONSISTENT error code of 0x13D (317) on multiple consecutive calls associated with this site (other, unrelated call sites elsewhere in the runtime returned 0x0) -- not a standard Win32 code immediately recognizable, and not documented anywhere in this project's existing native source. Named for r447: trace sub_821F4E70 deeper (it only calls a generic prologue helper in its own visible body, so the real logic sourcing this error is further down) to find the actual native host stub responsible for 0x13D, and resolve the pcVar19/iRam8293b94c table lookup to a concrete file/handle. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
